senses.gloss: f. (ἐξέδρα, exedra) (Greek) a covered place in front of the house; (Roman) recess, parlor, hall for conversations and discussions.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Judges 3:23">Targ. Jud. III, 23</cite>. [Pl.

<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 104:3">Targ. Ps. CIV, 3</cite>, v. <cite ref="A01371"><he>אִינְדְּרָא</he></cite>.] <cite ref="Bava Batra 11b:2">B. Bath. 11ᵇ</cite> <he>א׳ דבי רב</he> the hall of the school house (philosophers’ exedra, v. Sm. Ant. s. v.), contrad. to <he>א׳ רומייתא</he> (Ms. Oxf. <he>דרומיתא</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 10) Roman exedra (open but surrounded by a railing).

<cite ref="Bava Batra 25a:8">Ib. 25ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Bava Batra 25b:7">25ᵇ</cite> <he>עולם לא׳ וכ׳</he> the world resembles an exedra the northernmost side of which is not covered (<he>מסוככת</he> Ms. M., ed. <he>מסובבת</he> not surrounded); a. fr.—Pl. <he>אַכְסַדְרָאוֹת</he>.
<cite ref="Tamid 28b:13">Tam. 28ᵇ</cite> <he>א׳ של בנין</he> exedras forming, or belonging to, a structure (opp. to open exedra with plants).
